theoryContent:
Archimedes' Principle & Fluid Statics:
1. Archimedes' Principle: Any object completely or partially immersed in a fluid experiences an upward buoyant force equal to the weight of fluid displaced by the object: F_b = ρ_f · V_sub · g.
2. Floating Condition: When an object has lower density than the fluid (ρ_b < ρ_f), it floats with a submerged fraction equal to the density ratio: V_sub / V_total = ρ_b / ρ_f.
3. Sinking & Normal Force: When an object is denser than the fluid (ρ_b > ρ_f), it sinks to the bottom. Once resting on the tank floor, the normal reaction force is N = W - F_b.
4. Apparent Weight: A spring scale suspending a submerged object measures W_apparent = W - F_b, directly demonstrating the buoyant reduction in felt weight.
